LCM(20, 42, 76) = [latex]2^2\times3\times5\times7\times19=7980[/latex]. Remainder 7 in each case: 7980 + 7 = 7987.

questions.question: Consider a knock-out women's badminton singles tournament where there are no ties. The loser in each game is eliminated from the tournament. Every player plays until she is defeated or remains the last undefeated player. The last undefeated player is declared the winner of the tournament. If there are [latex]64[/latex] players in the beginning of the tournament, how many games should be played in total to declare the winner of the tournament?
questions.explanation:
This is a single-elimination (knock-out) tournament: every game has exactly one loser, and every loser is eliminated permanently. To determine a single overall winner among [latex]64[/latex] players, all [latex]63[/latex] of the other players must each lose exactly one game (and no player needs to lose more than once, since losing eliminates them).

So the number of games played [latex]=[/latex] number of players eliminated [latex]=64-1=63[/latex] (each game produces exactly one elimination).

Answer: 63

questions.question: If [latex]Pe^{x} = Q e^{-x} [/latex] for all real values of [latex]x [/latex], which one of the following statements is true?
questions.explanation:
[latex]Pe^x=Qe^{-x}[/latex] for every real [latex]x[/latex]. Multiply both sides by [latex]e^x[/latex]: [latex]Pe^{2x}=Q[/latex]. Since [latex]e^{2x}[/latex] genuinely varies with [latex]x[/latex] (it's not constant), the only way the left side can stay equal to the constant [latex]Q[/latex] for every [latex]x[/latex] is if the coefficient [latex]P[/latex] itself is [latex]0[/latex]. With [latex]P=0[/latex], the equation becomes [latex]0=Q[/latex], so [latex]Q=0[/latex] too.

Checking directly at [latex]x=0[/latex]: [latex]P=Q[/latex]. Combined with the "must hold for all [latex]x[/latex]" requirement, [latex]P=Q=0[/latex] is the only consistent solution.

Answer: P = Q = 0

questions.question: A plot of land must be divided between four families. They want their individual plots to be similar in shape, not necessarily equal in area. The land has equally spaced poles, marked as dots in the below figure. Two ropes, R1 and R2, are already present and cannot be moved. What is the least number of additional straight ropes needed to create the desired plots? A single rope can pass through three poles that are aligned in a straight line.
questions.explanation:
Take the poles as a 7 [latex]\times[/latex] 7 grid (0-6). R1 runs from the left edge (0, 2) to (2, 2), R2 from the top edge (4, 6) to (4, 4). The land is symmetric about both diagonals, and R1, R2 are mirror images.

Add 3 ropes:
1. (2, 0) to (2, 2) [latex]\text{---}[/latex] mirror of R1
2. (6, 4) to (4, 4) [latex]\text{---}[/latex] mirror of R2
3. (2, 2) to (4, 4) [latex]\text{---}[/latex] diagonal through the centre pole (3, 3)

This gives two small plots (a 2[latex]\times[/latex]2 square with one corner cut) and two large plots (a 4[latex]\times[/latex]4 square with one corner cut). The large ones are exactly the small ones scaled by 2, so all four are similar. Two ropes cannot do this.

Answer: 3

questions.question: The variable cost [latex](V)[/latex] of manufacturing a product varies according to the equation [latex]V=4q[/latex], where [latex]q[/latex] is the quantity produced. The fixed cost ([latex]F[/latex]) of production of same product reduces with q according to the equation [latex]F=\frac{100}{q}[/latex]. How many units should be produced to minimize the total cost [latex](V+F)[/latex]?
questions.explanation:
Total cost C = 4q + 100/q.

[latex]\frac{dC}{dq}=4-\frac{100}{q^2}=0\Rightarrow q^2=25\Rightarrow q=5[/latex]

Answer: 5

questions.question: A transporter receives the same number of orders each day. Currently, he has some pending orders (backlog) to be shipped. If he uses 7 trucks, then at the end of the 4th day he can clear all the orders. Alternatively, if he uses only 3 trucks, then all the orders are cleared at the end of the 10th day. What is the minimum number of trucks required so that there will be no pending order at the end of 5th day?
questions.explanation:
Let backlog = B, new orders per day = d, one truck clears c orders per day.
- 7 [latex]\times[/latex] 4c = B + 4d
- 3 [latex]\times[/latex] 10c = B + 10d

Subtracting: 2c = 6d [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] c = 3d, and B = 80d.

For 5 days: N [latex]\times[/latex] 5 [latex]\times[/latex] 3d [latex]\ge[/latex] 80d + 5d [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] N [latex]\ge[/latex] 5.67 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 6 trucks

Answer: 6
